The NCE Programme Unit works to advance integrated, forward-looking solutions that strengthen resilience, promote sustainable development pathways, and support Belize in addressing the growing impacts of climate change and ecosystem degradation. UNDP supports national partners in designing and implementing programmes that move beyond short-term interventions toward systemic change, combining policy support, institutional strengthening, and investment solutions. Within this framework, the Biodiversity Finance Initiative (BIOFIN) is a global partnership led by UNDP that supports countries to address the biodiversity finance challenge through a structured, evidence-based methodology. BIOFIN aims to assess biodiversity finance needs and gaps, identify opportunities for resource mobilization, and develop and implement finance solutions that increase investment in biodiversity, improve efficiency of expenditures, and reduce harmful financial flows. The BIOFIN programme in Belize is implemented in close collaboration with the Government of Belize, particularly the National Biodiversity Office (NBIO), which serves as the national coordinating body responsible for advancing implementation of the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025–2035. The NBSAP outlines national targets for biodiversity conservation, restoration, and sustainable use, and emphasizes the need for strengthened financing mechanisms to support implementation at scale. Under BIOFIN Belize, key activities follow the global methodology and include Biodiversity Finance Policy and Institutional Review (PIR), Biodiversity Expenditure Review (BER), Financial Needs Assessment (FNA), and Development and implementation of the Biodiversity Finance Plan (BFP). These components collectively support the identification and prioritization of finance solutions that align national biodiversity targets with sustainable finance strategies, while contributing to relevant Sustainable Development Goals, including climate action and life on land. As the programme transitions to a new phase, BIOFIN Belize is undergoing a restructuring to respond to evolving funding constraints and to strengthen its focus on implementation and scaling of biodiversity finance solutions. Support the UNDP CO to ensure compliance with UNDP administrative, financial, and procurement procedures. Organize and lead regular national team meetings and coordinate engagement with the BIOFIN Global Team through scheduled calls and technical exchanges. Ensure clear communication, coordination, and collaboration within the project team and among all partners. Planning, Monitoring, Reporting, and Knowledge Management Signal any delays in national deliverables compared to the workplan to the UNDP Country Office. Develop workshop reports for all technical workshops. Develop briefing notes, case studies, press releases, web articles and other media products as required. Assist with research and write and edit sections of technical reports as required. Review all national level deliverables to ensure quality and consistency with the BIOFIN methodology. Stakeholder Engagement, Advocacy, and Resource Mobilization Organize and facilitate stakeholder consultations, workshops, and dialogues in a participatory and inclusive manner. Institutional Arrangement Under the overall guidance of the UNDP Belize Country Office and with direct supervision of the Programme Lead for the Nature, Climate and Energy Portfolio, the National Coordinator will be responsible for the day-to-day management, coordination and implementation of the BIOFIN Programme activities in Belize. The Renewables team originates and executes in the order of $1 billion a year, and this role sits at the centre of that activity, taking transactions from structuring through to financial close. Reporting to a Head of Platform, you will take day-to-day carriage of assigned transactions as well as working on some origination activities. Execution is the heart of the role : you will develop investment structures and negotiate terms, lead the legal, financial and technical due diligence, prepare credit assessments and investment papers, manage the CEFC approval process and drive documentation through to close. Most deals fall between $100-200 million and the CEFC invests across the capital structure. You will typically lead one transaction in execution at a time, working in a deal team of two alongside and supervising a senior associate or associate, alongside a wider, collaborative transaction support team. For many transactions, you will also hold the client relationship. You will be the point person with sponsors, advisers, co-financiers and counterparties, and will contribute to the industry and strategic work that shapes where the CEFC invests next. Based in our Sydney office, you will join a small, flat and highly collaborative team where origination, market intelligence and insight are shared openly across the group. The role requires travel between the CEFC's offices and to other cities and states as and when required. This is a rewarding opportunity to apply deep transaction skills to Australia's energy transition, at a point in the cycle when the pipeline of new renewable energy projects is growing. The role you’ll play As Associate Director, you will: Take day-to-day project management and execution carriage of assigned renewables transactions through to financial close. Develop investment structures and negotiate terms across the capital structure, including senior debt, mezzanine debt and equity funding, either directly or via existing or newly established funds. Undertake credit and risk analysis of investment opportunities, prepare investment papers and manage the CEFC approval process. Lead due diligence and documentation through to financial close, engaging internal and external lawyers, advisers and due diligence providers. Support and deliver business development and origination activities, contributing to the development, structuring and evaluation of investment opportunities across the renewables platform. Collaborate across the Investment team on strategic insights and future investment focus areas, identifying and considering financing opportunities across the market. Leverage industry contacts to develop financial products and investment opportunities, and influence the development and implementation of the CEFC product suite. Maintain client and counterparty relationships, ensuring deliverables under customer contracts are met and providing a structured customer review process. Report on origination and transaction pipelines, and capture and disseminate project knowledge internally and externally, including through case studies and other educational and promotional material. Lead transaction teams, coaching and mentoring junior colleagues by sharing knowledge and expertise across the CEFC's sector platforms. To be successful in this role, you will bring: Seven or more years of demonstrated experience in structuring, negotiating and executing transactions, gained in commercial banking, funds management, financial advisory, direct equity or the private credit division of an institutional investment group or other financial institution, with a track record of taking transactions through to financial close. Strong transactional skills, including developing key investment terms and investment structures, identifying risks, and undertaking due diligence, financial analysis and modelling, valuation, credit analysis and the preparation of transaction documentation and investment papers. Experience with a broad range of finance structures and with corporate and project risk assessment and management. Project or structured finance experience in renewables, energy or infrastructure is highly relevant. Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex concepts to internal audiences such as investment committee and board, and to external audiences such as sponsors, advisers and other market participants. A solution-focused approach, working with urgency and creativity to solve problems as they arise, and the ability to think beyond the limits and take on a long-term perspective. Organised and effective in high pressure situations, planning ahead to manage to tight deadlines and taking ownership of the outcome. The ability to work well in a highly collaborative, people-centred environment, building trust and confidence within the team and with senior management. Previous people leadership experience is preferred. Relevant tertiary qualifications in finance, commerce, mathematics, engineering, actuarial studies or a related quantitative discipline. Are you ready to contribute to the achievement of Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets? If you're someone who’s driven to make a positive impact, exploring new frontiers, overcoming challenges and seizing opportunities, then the CEFC could be the place for you.
